summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral below-knee amputations, and a history of multidrug-resistant urinary tract infections was admitted with fevers to 103 and chills. She was found to have a urinary tract infection caused by carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae, which was treated with intravenous meropenem after initial broad-spectrum coverage. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic completion. During admission, stool was noted in the vaginal vault, prompting evaluation for a rectovaginal fistula; however, MRI and colonoscopy showed no fistula or mass. Left stump infection was assessed with ultrasound, which showed no abscess, and vascular surgery recommended outpatient follow-up. Acute kidney injury was monitored, with creatinine fluctuating but ultimately improving to 1.4. The patient was discharged home on oral vancomycin for C. diff prophylaxis, with follow-up planned in colorectal, vascular, and gynecology clinics.
